audit.whatIsWrong: The entire full layer is built around an ability called 'Repeating Dashes'. Ambessa has no such ability. It appears 23 times: tldr, winCon, enemyWin, focus.text, loading, ahead, phases[3].why, breakdown.early/mid/cooldowns/trading/spikes/feeding/difficulty, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[2].d, and report[1]/[3]/[5]/[9]/[10]/[12]/[13].
audit.why: Ambessa's real abilities are Drakehound's Step (P), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q), Repudiation (W), Lacerate (E) and Public Execution (R). 'Repeating Dashes' is fabricated. This is the same class of error as the calibration examples — and it is worse than a single mislabelled slot, because it is the matchup's tracked ability: focus.text, the loading screen, the cooldown breakdown and every Do card all point the player at something that does not exist. A Nasus following this page is told to track a cooldown he can never see.
audit.corrected: Renamed all 23 occurrences to Drakehound's Step, which is the ability the surrounding text is actually describing — the passive that turns any ability cast into a dash, i.e. the 'repeating dashes' the author had in mind. Riot's text: 'Entering an attack or movement command while casting an ability will cause Ambessa to dash a short distance once the ability is cast.'

audit.whatIsWrong: Repudiation is never mentioned in either layer, in a matchup where it is the single most important ability against this specific champion.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Ambessa gains a shield, briefly braces herself, and then slams the ground ... If she blocked any non-minion damage while bracing herself, this ability will deal increased damage.' Nasus's entire damage output is one large, telegraphed, animation-locked Siphoning Strike. Feeding a stacked Q into a braced Repudiation is the worst possible outcome in the matchup — the shield eats the hit AND the block powers up her counter-slam. Every other champion pays a smaller price for this mistake because their damage is spread across more instances; Nasus pays all of it at once. The correct sequencing is to make her spend Repudiation (18s at rank 1) and only then commit the Q.
audit.corrected: Added the wait-out-Repudiation rule to content.mid, whys[1] and breakdown.cooldowns, with the 18s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Public Execution is described only as 'her ult' and 'chain CC'; neither the suppression nor the targeting rule is stated.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Ambessa blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival.' Two things follow. First, it is a suppression, not an ordinary stun, so the 'chain CC' framing understates it. Second, it takes the FARTHEST champion in the line — so in a teamfight a front-standing Nasus is not the one it hits, and after lane the correct advice for a Nasus is the opposite of the usual 'stand in front'. The current text gives neither.
audit.corrected: Named Public Execution and its suppression in content.mid, whys[4] and spikes[1]. The farthest-target rule is reported in notes rather than forced into a fixed-length lane string — it is a teamfight positioning fact and there is no writable field about post-lane positioning with room for it.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns describes 'Ambessa Lacerate: A dash strike that can recast — her core mobility + dodge tool.' Lacerate is not a dash and has no recast.
audit.why: Lacerate whips her drakehounds around herself for damage and a slow at 325 range on a 13/12/11/10/9s cooldown. The dash people associate with it comes from Drakehound's Step being initiated from it, which then adds a second strike at the end of the dash — a different ability doing the moving. Calling Lacerate itself a recastable dash will make a Nasus wait for a cooldown that is not the one gating her mobility.
audit.corrected: Replaced the Lacerate line with Repudiation's real 18s rank-1 cooldown and the brace interaction, which is the cooldown a Nasus actually needs to count.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early says 'you have no Wither until level 3'.
audit.why: Wither is a basic ability available from level 2 if taken there, and the full layer's phases[1].why says 'Wither online' at Level 2. Same cross-layer contradiction found on the Aatrox and Akali entries — it appears to be a template-wide defect in this file, not a per-matchup one.
audit.corrected: Removed the level claim and replaced it with Repudiation, which is the actual reason her early trades win.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds source anywhere despite _missing-interactions.json flagging needs-antiheal for this exact pairing.
audit.why: Public Execution carries a heal flag, so her all-in refunds health at exactly the moment a Nasus is trying to survive it. The matchup is a long grinding duel once Nasus has items, which is the shape of fight where Grievous Wounds matters most.
audit.corrected: Added it to content.late, where the 2+ items grind is described.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] titled 'Farm Q stacks safely' is described as 'Ambessa wastes Repeating Dashes — commit the full pattern immediately'; dontsFull[1] titled 'Chase her dashes' is described as 'Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown'.
audit.why: The same paste defect present on Aatrox, Akali and Akshan. Four of four matchups audited so far carry it, so it is systematic across the Nasus file.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both to match their titles using real numbers — Lacerate's 325 radius and Wither's 700 range / 15s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'level chart contradicts data: Nasus wins 52.27% but the chart gives Ambessa 5/7 stages vs 1'.
audit.why: The chart is [Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Nasus] against a 52.27% Nasus win rate over 396 games. Giving the enemy five of seven stages in a lane Nasus wins outright overstates her.
audit.corrected: NOT PROPOSED AS AN EDIT — blocked by the length rule. 'Ambessa' is 7 characters and the alternatives 'Nasus' and 'Skill' are 5, a ratio of 0.714, so the applier rejects any such edit on length before comparing it. Same blocker as the Akshan entry. See notes.

edits.before: Ambessa owns these levels and you have to accept it — her dash-in combo and W damage beat your statless early Q, and you have no Wither until level 3 to punish her. Don't try to trade Q for Q; just last-hit with Siphoning Strike and use Spirit Fire from range to farm stacks and chip the wave without stepping into her combo. Hold E for the moment she dashes onto you so the lingering armor shred and DoT cost her something for committing.
edits.after: Ambessa owns these levels and you have to accept it — Lacerate and Cunning Sweep beat your statless early Q, and Repudiation shields whatever you throw back. Don't try to trade Q for Q; just last-hit with Siphoning Strike and use Spirit Fire from range to farm stacks and chip the wave without stepping inside her 325 radius. Hold Spirit Fire for the moment she dashes onto you so the lingering armor shred costs her something for committing.

edits.before: This is her best window, not yours. At 6 her chain CC plus ult is a real kill threat, so save Wither for the instant she dashes in — the movement and attack-speed slow strips her ability to weave and lets you walk away. Don't ult to chase her dashes; ult only to survive a committed all-in. You're playing not to die and hoarding stacks while she's stronger, accepting you concede the lane window through levels 4-6.
edits.after: This is her best window, not yours. At 6 Public Execution suppresses you into a full combo, so save Wither for the instant she dashes in — the attack-speed slow guts the empowered Drakehound's Step follow-up and lets you walk away. Never feed a stacked Q into a fresh Repudiation; bracing it both absorbs the hit and powers her slam, so make her spend it first. You're hoarding stacks and conceding the window through levels 4-6.

edits.before: Once you hit 2+ items the matchup flips hard. Your infinite Q stacks plus Fury of the Sands give you the burst and durability to win the sustained duel, and Wither is the answer to all her mobility — a withered Ambessa can't dash-kite away from your empowered Q, and Spirit Fire's armor shred plus your lifesteal grind her down. Get your stacks, land the slow, and you out-scale the bruiser who bullied you early.
edits.after: Once you hit 2+ items the matchup flips hard. Your infinite Q stacks plus Fury of the Sands give you the burst and durability to win the sustained duel, and Wither is the answer to all her mobility — a withered Ambessa can't dash-kite away from your empowered Q, and Spirit Fire's armor shred plus your lifesteal grind her down. Bring Grievous Wounds for the healing on Public Execution, then land the slow and out-scale her.

notes: HEADLINE: the fabricated ability 'Repeating Dashes' drove this entire matchup page, including focus.text and the loading screen, across 23 strings. Ambessa has no such ability. I mapped it to Drakehound's Step because that is what the surrounding prose describes, but the user should sanity-check that choice once — if the intended tracked ability was really Public Execution or Repudiation, the fix is a different name in the same 23 places and the rename edits can be regenerated mechanically. Worth grepping the whole repo for 'Repeating Dashes' and for other invented names on champions released around the same time; a generator that invented one name for Ambessa probably invented others. BLOCKED BY THE LENGTH RULE: the flagged chart defect (5/7 stages to Ambessa against a 52.27% Nasus win rate) cannot be proposed, because 'Ambessa' is 7 characters and 'Nasus'/'Skill' are 5 — ratio 0.714, rejected on length. The same blocker hit the Akshan entry. Enum-valued fields like win[] and phases[].side need exempting from the +/-10% band or these charts can never be corrected for any champion whose name is not exactly five letters. NOT ASSERTED, needs a wiki pass: Public Execution suppresses, and whether QSS or Cleanse breaks a suppression is not answerable from the kit file (needsResearch.cleansable is null) — I stated the suppression itself, which is in Riot's text, and made no claim about breaking it. Also left alone: whether Wither's slow is reduced by tenacity, and whether Repudiation's grounding matters here (it does not — Nasus has no dash, so per the relevance rule I wrote nothing about it). REPORTED BUT NOT EDITED: Public Execution 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line', so after lane a front-standing Nasus is not the one it hits — good teamfight positioning advice, but no writable field covers post-lane positioning with room to state it. No WKM_LINES problems seen for this pairing.
